name: HIAS Economic Advancement Fund — Refugee Entrepreneur Microloans
description: The HIAS Economic Advancement Fund (EAF) is a nonprofit Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) that provides refugees and other forcibly displaced entrepreneurs with access to affordable capital and business support services so they can launch and grow businesses in the United States. Operating through affiliate partners in twelve metropolitan areas, the EAF offers microloans, business technical assistance and training, financial and credit education, and market access facilitation. The fund specifically serves refugee, asylee, and Special Immigrant Visa holder entrepreneurs who face barriers to traditional bank financing due to limited U.S. credit history, language challenges, or unfamiliarity with the American financial system. In partnership with The Braun Foundation and other funders, the EAF has provided thousands of dollars in direct grants for refugee-owned businesses, including hurricane recovery support and startup capital. All services are culturally and linguistically responsive.
eligibility: Refugees, asylees, Special Immigrant Visa holders, and other forcibly displaced individuals in the United States who are starting or growing a business; must be located in or near one of the 12 participating metro areas; no minimum credit score required
amount: Microloans and business grants — amounts vary by program and partner location; recent grant rounds have awarded $2,000–$10,000 per business
applicationProcess: Contact the HIAS Economic Advancement Fund through hiaseaf.org or reach out to your local HIAS affiliate office. Applicants undergo an intake assessment and may be referred to business training programs before loan approval. The EAF evaluates business viability and character rather than traditional credit scores. Technical assistance and financial literacy workshops are provided alongside lending.
geographicScope: United States — 12 metropolitan areas through HIAS affiliate partners (including New York, New Jersey, Los Angeles, San Diego, and others)
documentsRequired: Proof of immigration status (refugee, asylee, SIV documentation); business plan or concept; personal identification; financial statements if available; proof of residence in a participating metro area

name: Kiva U.S. 0% Interest Crowdfunded Microloans for Entrepreneurs
description: Kiva U.S. offers crowdfunded microloans of up to $15,000 at 0% interest to small business owners and entrepreneurs in the United States who lack access to traditional bank credit. Unlike conventional lenders, Kiva uses a social lending model where individual lenders from around the world fund loans in $25 increments. Borrowers create a public loan profile describing their business and funding needs, then invite friends, family, and community members to start lending — once the loan reaches a certain threshold of community support, it is opened to all Kiva lenders worldwide. The program is particularly valuable for immigrant entrepreneurs because Kiva does not require a minimum credit score, does not check credit history, and accepts ITIN (Individual Taxpayer Identification Number) holders. Loans are repaid over terms of up to 36 months with no interest or fees charged by Kiva. Over $2 billion in loans have been disbursed globally through the Kiva platform.
eligibility: U.S.-based entrepreneurs and small business owners aged 18+; no minimum credit score; accepts ITIN in place of SSN; must be able to demonstrate community support by recruiting initial lenders from personal network; business can be at any stage including pre-revenue startups
amount: Up to $15,000 at 0% interest; repaid over up to 36 months
applicationProcess: Create a borrower profile on kiva.org/borrow describing your business and how the loan will be used. Invite at least 5–10 people from your personal network to lend to your loan (this demonstrates community support). Once the loan reaches a participation threshold, it is listed publicly for all Kiva lenders. Fully funded loans are disbursed to your bank account. Repayments are made monthly over the agreed term.
geographicScope: United States — nationwide; borrowers must have a U.S. bank account
documentsRequired: Government-issued ID or ITIN; U.S. bank account; business description and photos; no formal business plan required

name: Grameen America Microloans for Women Entrepreneurs
description: Grameen America is a nonprofit microfinance organization that provides microloans, financial training, and asset-building support to low-income women entrepreneurs in the United States, many of whom are immigrants. Founded on the principles of Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus's Grameen Bank model, the organization serves women who lack credit history, collateral, or access to traditional banking. Grameen America has served over 150,000 women and disbursed more than $4 billion in loans since its founding. The program operates through a group lending model — borrowers form groups of five women who meet weekly for financial education and mutual accountability. Loans start small (as low as $500) and increase as borrowers build credit history and demonstrate repayment. The program also offers savings accounts, financial literacy workshops, and credit-building tools. Grameen America operates in over 20 cities across the United States.
eligibility: Low-income women entrepreneurs in the United States; no credit score requirement; no collateral required; must be willing to participate in a five-member lending group and attend weekly center meetings; open to immigrants regardless of documentation status in most locations
amount: Starting at $500; loans increase with successful repayment up to $15,000+; interest rates are below market rate
applicationProcess: Contact a local Grameen America branch in one of the 20+ participating cities. Form or join a five-member lending group of women entrepreneurs. Attend orientation and financial training sessions. Submit a loan application through your branch. Loans are disbursed after group formation and initial training. Weekly center meetings are required throughout the loan term for financial education and group accountability.
geographicScope: United States — 20+ cities including New York, Los Angeles, Houston, Charlotte, Indianapolis, Austin, Newark, and others
documentsRequired: Government-issued photo ID (accepts foreign passports and consular IDs); proof of address; proof of income or business activity; no SSN required in most locations (ITIN accepted)

name: France French Tech Visa for Startup Founders
description: The French Tech Visa is a fast-track, simplified residence permit for international startup founders, investors, and employees who want to join or build companies in the French tech ecosystem. Introduced by the French government as part of the La French Tech initiative, the visa provides a four-year renewable residence permit (Passeport Talent) that covers the founder and their family. Startup founders must be supported by a French Tech-accredited incubator, accelerator, or venture capital fund. The program is designed to attract global entrepreneurial talent to France and provides access to one of Europe's largest startup ecosystems with over 30,000 startups. France also offers complementary programs including the French Tech Ticket, which provides up to EUR 57,000 in funding (EUR 25,000 for professional services and the remainder for personal expenses and incubator fees), workspace in a partner incubator, and mentorship. The visa application process is streamlined and typically takes 2–4 weeks for endorsed candidates.
eligibility: International entrepreneurs with an innovative tech startup project; must be endorsed by a French Tech-accredited organization (incubator, accelerator, or VC fund); no minimum investment required for the visa; French Tech Ticket applicants must apply through designated incubator partners
amount: French Tech Visa: no direct funding (provides residence permit); French Tech Ticket: up to EUR 57,000 in funding per team (EUR 25,000 for professional services + remainder for personal expenses and incubator fees)
applicationProcess: Identify and apply to a French Tech-accredited incubator, accelerator, or VC fund for endorsement. Once endorsed, apply for the Passeport Talent visa through the French consulate in your country. The visa process is streamlined for endorsed candidates and typically takes 2–4 weeks. For French Tech Ticket: apply through designated partner incubators during open application periods. Selected teams receive funding, workspace, and mentorship.
geographicScope: France — nationwide; primary startup ecosystems in Paris, Lyon, Toulouse, Bordeaux, and Marseille
documentsRequired: Valid passport; endorsement letter from a French Tech-accredited organization; business plan; proof of financial means for initial settlement; health insurance; for French Tech Ticket: team composition, startup pitch, and incubator acceptance
